suggestions.quote: an email, OFFER, and a big ACCEPT button
suggestions.fix: Written words OFFER and ACCEPT break the on-screen text rule. Draw an envelope icon and a green tick button with no lettering. If a word is needed, make it one stamped tag, 'OFFER'. Keep the thumb and the button clear of faces.

suggestions.quote: The same doorway through the seasons, a second or two each
suggestions.fix: This hold runs 7 s, over the 6 s limit, and it is not the one wordless peak (line 148). Trim it to 6 s at 1.5 s per season. Keep the flaps 260, 259, 258, 257 ticking on each arrival so something moves every 2 to 4 s.

suggestions.quote: The train crosses fields at dusk; your face at the window, phone dark in your lap.
suggestions.fix: The cue sheet ends 'The first jump' music at 'Home. Obviously.' and starts 'The first weekend' music at 'You thought it would drop', so this 2 s hold plays with no music. That would be a third unplanned silence, and the limit is two. In `cues.yaml`, move the first jump's `music_out` to the end of this hold, or carry the city cue under the hold and let the home cue come in on the porch clack.

suggestions.quote: The montage stops on winter, by Grandpa's chair.
suggestions.fix: Grandpa's counter reads 8 at line 74 and is never seen again, although you now visit weekly and mom's counter climbs to 260. Show his counter flipping upward (8 to a bigger number) as he starts the story. It keeps continuity and pays off the weekly visits.

suggestions.quote: You didn't have to imagine it. You had a number.
suggestions.fix: Lines 169 to 172 are a narration stretch with a fact line and no new picture after the hold. Add a SCENE: an insert on Grandpa's flipping counter, then a close on your face with a small smile, so the c04 line lands on a changing image.

suggestions.quote: It wasn't her clock. It was your timetable.
suggestions.fix: Add a SCENE after the 9 s peak: a slow push-in on 260 with a brief paper-ghost trail of the train timetable (train icons only, no text) sliding past. The reveal line then has a picture and the stage is not left on the peak frame.

In `cues.yaml` the third jump carries one intent, 'tense', from 'Train.' to 'You had a number.', but the story turns warm after the peak (dal, montage, Grandpa). Split it: 'tense' to the flip at 'Next Friday.', then a 'warm' cue entering at or after 'It only counted down because you only ever planned less'. That keeps the change at or after the reveal.

suggestions.quote: The porch at dusk. Mom at the door with a glass of chai, steam rising.
suggestions.fix: Reuse list. Build one porch/door set and swap moods (dusk, night, lamp, day) for lines 17, 68, 120, 141 and 176. Reuse the platform set for the home-city station (line 83, already planned). Reuse the office set for the meeting room and the night office, with the footbridge as a window layer. Reuse the rented-room set for the napkin and the self-drawing strip. New builds are then the auto and lane, the metro pole, the carriage cutaway and the dinner table. Keep each to flat layers.

suggestions.quote: a counter over every head on the lane: the neighbour watering plants, the paan stall, the kid on a cycle.
suggestions.fix: Limit this to three or four figures with counters and let the rest of the lane be a blank flat layer, as line 44 does. That keeps the build small and the counters readable.

suggestions.quote: You look at the train app, then the pillow.
suggestions.fix: Show the app as a train-icon screen with no text, so the only words on screen stay tags, counters and bubbles.

keep.quote: You thought it would drop when you left. It drops when you walk in.
It wasn't her clock. It was your timetable.
She's still at the door. Of course she is.
